The proposed answer of 70° is incorrect; a direct numerical computation gives ∠APC ≈ 74°.

**Flaw in the proposed solution.** Step 1 claims AP = AQ follows from BP = QC and AB = AC. It does not. Triangles ABP and ACQ have the same two sides but different included angles at A (20° versus 26°), so they are not congruent and nothing forces AP = AQ.

**Numerical check.** Place A at the origin with AB = AC = 1, and let ∠BAC = 92°. Put B on the ray at 0°, P at distance p along 20°, Q at distance q along 66°, and C along 92°.

The conditions BP = QC and BP = PQ become:
- p² − 2p·cos20° = q² − 2q·cos26°
- q² − 2pq·cos46° = 1 − 2p·cos20°

Solving gives p ≈ 0.5816 and q ≈ 0.669, so AP ≠ AQ.

With these values, P ≈ (0.5465, 0.1989) and C ≈ (−0.0349, 0.9994).

Then PA = (−0.5465, −0.1989) and PC = (−0.5814, 0.8005).

cos∠APC = (PA·PC)/(|PA||PC|) ≈ 0.1585 / (0.5816 × 0.9893) ≈ 0.2755, so ∠APC ≈ 74°.

VERDICT: REJECT
